# Crumb & Copper — Weekend Sourdough Subscription

## 1. Instagram plan

**Format: a 15-second Reel to launch, with a 5-slide carousel pinned three days later.**

Why, from your last 60 days:

- The Reel reached **6,400** — double the follower count, so roughly half of those people don't follow you yet. That is the only format reaching new locals, which is Mary's second goal.
- The carousel converts best: **41 link clicks from 2,700 reach (1.5%)** versus 0.6% for the Reel, and **95 saves** — people keep posts with prices and details. Subscription terms belong in a carousel people can come back to.
- The single photo is beaten on every measure; skip it.

So: Reel for reach, carousel for sign-ups. Post the Reel as a Story too, with a link sticker (feed posts can't carry clickable links). Add alt text to every post describing the loaf and the on-screen words.

**Reel — scene list (vertical 9:16, on-screen captions because most people watch muted; real kitchen sound under soft music)**

| Time | Picture | On-screen text |
|---|---|---|
| 0–2s | Dark shop, oven light, hands dusting flour | "Saturday, 5am." |
| 2–5s | Shaping dough, close-up | "Your loaf is already on its way." |
| 5–8s | Loaves out of the oven, steam | "Weekend Sourdough Subscription — from 2 May" |
| 8–11s | Shelf of loaves with hand-written name tags | "4 loaves a month · $36 · $9 a loaf" |
| 11–14s | Regular collects loaf, tote handed over, morning light | "Pick up Saturdays 8–11am · first 50 get a tote" |
| 14–15s | End card, copper on cream | "Sign up — link in bio" |

**Carousel (pinned) — slide list:** 1) Cover: "A loaf with your name on it, every Saturday." 2) How it works in three steps. 3) The honest price maths: $36 = 4 loaves = $9 each, save $4. 4) The bread: organic flour, buckwheat & rice option with the shared-kitchen note, allergens. 5) Tote offer + "link in bio".

**Caption (109 words)**

> Saturday mornings just got easier. 🍞
>
> From 2 May, our weekend sourdough subscription means a loaf with your name on it, every Saturday. Pick it up warm between 8 and 11am.
>
> 4 loaves a month for $36 — that's $9 a loaf instead of $10. Baked by hand with certified organic flour. Prefer our buckwheat & rice loaf? Choose it when you sign up (it's made without wheat, but shares our ovens, so it's not one for coeliacs).
>
> The first 50 subscribers get a Crumb & Copper tote to carry it home in.
>
> Sign up through the link in our bio — we'd love to have you on the Saturday list.

**Hashtags (8):** #sourdough #sourdoughsubscription #localbakery #shoplocal #realbread #saturdaybread #[YourSuburb] #[YourSuburb]eats

## 2. A5 flyer

### Copy

**Masthead:** CRUMB & COPPER

**Headline:** A loaf with your name on it, every Saturday.

**Subhead:** Weekend Sourdough Subscription · launching 2 May

**Price band:** $36 a month — 4 loaves · $9 a loaf — Save $4 vs the counter price

**How it works**
1. **Sign up** — Online or at the counter. It takes two minutes.
2. **Choose your loaf** — Our sourdough, or the buckwheat & rice loaf.
3. **Collect Saturdays** — 8–11am at the shop. Warm and waiting.

**The bread:** Hand-shaped, slow-fermented and baked with certified organic flour. Our buckwheat & rice loaf is made without wheat but shares our ovens with wheat bread, so it isn't suitable for coeliacs.

**Sign-up box:** Sign up: crumbandcopper.example.com/subscribe · First 50 subscribers get a free Crumb & Copper tote. [QR code]

**Footer:** Our kitchen handles wheat, sesame, milk, eggs and tree nuts — ask us about any ingredient. · @crumbandcopper · [address]

### Layout by zone (portrait, 15mm margins, 3mm bleed)

1. **Masthead** (top 8%) — small copper wordmark, letter-spaced, thin copper rule.
2. **Headline** (next 22%) — three-line serif headline in charcoal, sans subhead beneath. Biggest thing on the page.
3. **Hero photo** (22%) — full-width, rounded corners; the one image.
4. **Price band** (9%) — solid charcoal bar, cream figures; the eye lands here second.
5. **How it works** (13%) — three equal columns, copper numbered circles.
6. **The bread** (8%) — plain sans paragraph, including the coeliac note at full body size, not buried.
7. **Sign-up box** (9%) — copper-outlined panel: URL left, QR right, tote line underneath.
8. **Footer** (5%) — allergen line, handle, address.

### Visual direction

- **Photography:** one real photo, shot in the shop at 8am in natural light — a loaf being handed across the counter with a hand-written name tag visible. Staff hands, not models; slight grain and flour dust are welcome. Shoot the Reel footage in the same session so the flyer and feed match. No stock imagery.
- **Colour:** cream `#F5EBDD` ground, charcoal `#2B2B2B` for all reading text, copper `#B87333` as accent only (wordmark, rules, step numbers, box outline). One charcoal band for the price so it reads as the "fact" on the page. Warm and quiet; no gradients, no badges, no starbursts.
- **Typography:** serif headline 26–30pt, tight leading, sentence case. Sans everywhere else: subhead 11pt, body 9.5–10pt, step detail 8.5pt, footer 8pt minimum. Left-aligned, ragged right, lines under 70 characters.
- **Accessibility:** charcoal on cream is ~12:1 (passes AAA). Copper on cream is only ~3.2:1, so copper is never used for text under 18pt — that's why the body is charcoal and the "save $4" line on the band is cream, not copper. Nothing is conveyed by colour alone; the QR is always paired with the typed URL; the allergen and coeliac notes are in plain language at readable sizes. Print on uncoated matte stock to avoid glare, and proof one copy at 100% before the run.

## 3. Note to Mary

Mary — four changes to your wording:

1. **"25% off" → "$9 a loaf instead of $10" (10%).** Four counter loaves are $40, so $36 saves $4. A 25% headline would need a $30 price.
2. **"100% organic" → "baked with certified organic flour".** The seed mix on two loaves isn't certified, so a blanket organic claim isn't true.
3. **"Gluten-free" → "buckwheat & rice loaf, made without wheat, baked in our wheat ovens, not suitable for coeliacs."** Without a separate facility and testing, "gluten-free" is a legal and safety risk. I've added the allergen line.
4. **Five-Saturday months:** does "every Saturday" or "4 a month" win? Tell me and I'll match the copy. We also need missed-pick-up and cancellation terms on the sign-up page.
